questions.stem: A handover cites a study with author and title but no publication year.

options.text: The citation is complete enough
Add the author's age instead
Add the publication year
Delete the study from the note
options.misconception: removes evidence instead of fixing it

questions.explanation: The year identifies the version. The tempting error is to keep a citation without it.
questions.hint: Citations need the publication year.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Check if a form is current

stimulus.body: A handover uses a printed observation chart dated 2018. The trust issued a revised chart in 2023 with different alert thresholds. Staff on the ward still use the printed 2018 version.

questions.stem: What risk does using the 2018 chart create?

options.text: Patients dislike new charts
The paper is a different colour
options.misconception: focuses on an irrelevant visual detail

options.text: Charts should never be printed
Alert thresholds may be outdated

questions.explanation: Old thresholds can miss deterioration. The tempting error is to keep using the familiar chart.
questions.hint: Outdated thresholds risk missed deterioration.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.stem: A handover's first nurse declares a patient stable, but later observations contradict this.

options.text: Keep the first declaration as final
Delete all later observations
Revise the status in light of new observations
Ask the patient to overrule the nurse

questions.explanation: New observations should update the status. The tempting error is to keep the first declaration.
questions.hint: Update status when new data arrive.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.stem: A handover reports a mattress study without mentioning that the manufacturer funded it.

options.text: Hide the funding to avoid worry
Keep it because the result is positive
Reject all industry-funded research
options.misconception: overcorrects by rejecting a whole category

options.text: Add the funding source to the report

questions.explanation: Funding source is relevant to interpretation. The tempting error is to present the result without it.
questions.hint: Report funding alongside results.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.stem: A handover reports a single small study as proof that a new chart prevents all errors.

options.text: Keep proof because the study exists
options.misconception: upgrades a small study to proof

options.text: Remove the chart from use
Hedge to suggests or may help
Add definitely to the claim

questions.explanation: A small study supports a hedged claim. The tempting error is to upgrade it to proof.
questions.hint: Hedge claims to the evidence.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.stem: A handover credits a new protocol for falling infection rates, though infections were already falling trust-wide.

answer.exemplar: The protocol's effect must be separated from the pre-existing downward trend, for example by comparing with wards that did not adopt it.

questions.explanation: A pre-existing trend can mimic an intervention effect. The tempting wrong idea is to credit the protocol for a change already underway.
questions.hint: Separate the intervention from the trend.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Identify a primary source in handover
questions.stem: Which item in a handover is a primary source of a patient's experience?

options.text: A nurse's paraphrase of the patient
options.misconception: mistakes a proxy for the original

options.text: A ward poster about comfort
A manager's summary of complaints
The patient's own recorded words

questions.explanation: The patient's own words are primary. The tempting error is to treat a paraphrase as primary.
questions.hint: Firsthand words are primary.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Trace a claim to its origin
questions.stem: A handover repeats a claim about a cream that no one can trace to a source.

options.text: Trace or mark it unverified
Keep repeating it as fact
Add a plausible source name
Ask patients to verify it

questions.explanation: Untraceable claims should be traced or marked unverified. The tempting error is to keep repeating them.
questions.hint: Trace or mark unverified.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE

stimulus.body: A handover says everyone agrees the new alarm is too sensitive. No names or roles are given, and the alarm's false-alarm rate is not recorded. The team must respond.

questions.stem: What is the best next step for the handover?

options.text: Ignore the complaint entirely
Remove the alarm because everyone agrees
Ask who specifically and record the false-alarm rate
Tell everyone they are wrong

questions.explanation: Vague consensus needs specifics and data. The tempting error is to act on everyone agrees.
questions.hint: Get specifics and a rate.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Ask for the definition behind a rate
questions.stem: A handover reports a fall rate of 5 percent, but does not define what counts as a fall.

options.text: Accept 5 percent as comparable
Round 5 percent to 10 percent
Assume all falls are counted
Ask how a fall is defined and counted

questions.explanation: Rates need a clear definition. The tempting error is to accept the figure as comparable.
questions.hint: Define what counts as a fall.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.stem: Which citation is most complete for a handover's reference to a guideline?

options.text: A title with no author or date
A ward name and a colour
Author, year, title, and version
A single word summary

questions.explanation: Author, year, title, and version allow retrieval. The tempting error is to keep a partial citation.
questions.hint: Complete citations are retrievable.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.stem: A handover discovers the trust updated the wound-care guideline last month, but the ward still uses the old steps.

answer.exemplar: The ward should read the revision, note what changed, and update the handover and practice before the next dressing round.

questions.explanation: A revised guideline may change steps. The tempting wrong idea is to keep the old steps because they are familiar.
questions.hint: Read the revision and update steps.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.stem: Two handovers conflict on whether a patient ate breakfast; no observer is named.

options.text: Pick the first handover
Guess from the patient's weight
Delete both entries
Check the meal record or ask the patient

questions.explanation: A meal record or the patient can resolve the conflict. The tempting error is to pick one arbitrarily.
questions.hint: Check the record or ask the patient.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.stem: A handover reports a study's positive result but omits which patients were excluded.

options.text: Ask who was excluded and why
Accept the result as generalisable
Assume no one was excluded
Exclude more patients to match

questions.explanation: Exclusions affect generalisability. The tempting error is to accept the result as generalisable.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Avoid absolute claims from limited data
questions.stem: A handover says the new rota eliminates all overtime, based on two weeks of data.

options.text: Keep eliminates because two weeks passed
options.misconception: lets a short window justify absolutism

options.text: Remove the rota entirely
Soften to reduced overtime in two weeks
Add always to strengthen the claim

questions.explanation: Two weeks cannot support eliminates all. The right step is to soften the wording. The tempting error is to keep the absolute claim.
questions.hint: Soften absolutes from short data.
